sections.text: Your due date is the date 280 days (40 weeks) after the first day of your last menstrual period, and our calculator can work it out from three different starting points: that period, a conception date, or an IVF transfer date. If the starting dates are consistent, all three methods land on the same day. This guide walks one pregnancy through all three and then lays out the calendar of trimesters and week numbers that follows from the result.

Each method works back to an LMP-equivalent date and then adds 280 days. Take a pregnancy whose LMP was March 8, 2027. The conception date the calculator assumes is 14 days later, and a day-5 blastocyst transfer is assumed to happen 19 days after the LMP-equivalent date.

rows: Add 280 days (adjusted if cycle is not 28 days)
Subtract 14 days to find the LMP equivalent, then add 280 (same as adding 266)
Subtract 19 days, then add 280 (same as adding 261)

sections.text: All dates in this guide are computed with straight calendar arithmetic and assume a 28-day cycle unless stated. The conception and IVF rows only agree with the LMP row because the example was built that way; in a real pregnancy the dates come from different sources and may disagree by days, which is why your provider sets the final date.
What a different cycle length does

The cycle-length field applies only to the LMP method. For a 35-day cycle the calculator assumes ovulation about 7 days later than in a 28-day cycle and moves the due date by 7 days, from December 13, 2027 to December 20, 2027. A 24-day cycle moves it 4 days earlier, to December 9, 2027. If your cycles vary from month to month, the average is a weak guide, and the scan date matters more.

Providers count pregnancy weeks from the LMP, which is called gestational age. Fetal age counts from conception, roughly two weeks later. For this example, 12 weeks 0 days of gestational age is May 31, 2027, when the fetal age is about 10 weeks. "How many weeks pregnant am I?" always refers to gestational age. A person at 12w3d has completed 12 weeks and 3 days; they are in their 13th week, which is why week numbers can look off by one between sources.

The calculator divides the 280 days into three trimesters using fixed day counts. The boundaries below are the calculator's convention, and other sources may place them a few days differently, so follow your provider's dating for care decisions.

The calculator summarises the trimesters briefly: the first is organ formation, the second is growth and movement being felt, and the third is final growth and lung maturation. That is a general outline, not a schedule of what will happen to you. It also lists a first-trimester ultrasound window of 8 to 13 weeks, which here runs from May 3, 2027 to June 13, 2027.

The 37-week row marks the start of early term and the 39-week row the start of full term, using the term definitions published by the National Institute of Child Health and Human Development. Only the 40-week row is the due date, and most pregnancies end on a different day.

items: Using the date of intercourse or a positive test as the LMP. The LMP method needs the first day of your last period.
Entering a cycle length for a conception or IVF date. The calculator ignores it for those methods.
Counting weeks from conception. Providers use gestational age, so quote that.
Reading the trimester dates as medical milestones. They are a counting convention; your care schedule comes from your provider.
Treating the result as final. If you have an early ultrasound, the date from that scan may replace the calculator's LMP-based date.

sections.text: This calculator gives a general estimate and does not replace advice from your midwife or doctor, who will confirm your due date and plan your care.

sections.heading: Calculate Your Pregnancy Due Date
sections.body: Use our Due Date Calculator to get your estimated due date, current gestational age, and trimester schedule. Supports LMP, conception, and IVF dates with automatic cycle-length adjustment.
